notes.spike_s1: Measured 2026-10-14 on this host (Microsoft H264 Video Decoder MFT, software, High bf2 fixture, sample time = packet tag): strategy A - output pictures carry the INPUT sample time of their packet and leave in presentation order. Reel's pump (video::Forward::accept drains pending packets up to the matched tag) needs decode order, so B-frame streams are refused typed (Unsupported mf-reorder-needs-packet-timing, printed NOT_PROVEN) instead of losing pictures. Unblock = reel-owner change (P2 family): Forward matches a picture to its packet and drops only pending packets whose pts precede the picture (presentation-order rule), then the worker drops its decode-order check; outside this lane's reel authority (P1 only).

notes.ring_decision: Threshold written before measuring (scratchpad ring-threshold.txt, ~19:37Z): build the shared-memory ring only if the fastest path delivers 2160p 4:2:0 8-bit through the pipe at < 30 fps AND the pipe is shown to be the limit. Measured (release build; a first debug-build run measured the test's own debug SHA-256, ~13 MB/s, discarded): 2160p software 32.1 fps -> threshold not met -> no ring. Finding: all four runs sit near 340-400 MB/s regardless of resolution and path, which suggests the pipe plus copies bound throughput; 2160p60 (746 MB/s) would need the ring (later lane).
